Every sample inside the Charging residency is a charge current: BMS_I_Dc is not positive. This pins the direction, without which a lower bound on a signed current says nothing.

items.notes: EXPECTED VERDICT: PASS. VOCABULARY LIMITATION: rule.value is a number, so the criterion vocabulary cannot assert BMS_Derating_Fct == clamp((60 - BMS_T_Derate_Ref) / 5, 0, 1) directly, nor BMS_I_Dc >= -BMS_I_Chg_Lim. Both are decomposed into numeric bounds over windows keyed on the other signal, which pins the law at three points of the band and the limit at two points of its range rather than universally. C4 and C5 window on BMS_I_Chg_Lim rather than on temperature deliberately: BMS_03 reports the derating triple one tick late, so the published limit and the current on the bus describe the same instant, while a window on BMS_T_Derate_Ref would straddle the 100 ms actuation delay and see up to 3 A of apparent excess during the steep part of the ramp.
items.objective: Show that the published derating factor follows clamp((T_batt_max - T_ref) / T_batt_safety_threshold, 0, 1) across the 55 degC to 60 degC band, and that the derated charge-current limit is the bound the charging current actually respects.

pass_criteria.description: Below the safety band the factor is unity: every sample where BMS_T_Derate_Ref is at or below T_batt_max minus T_batt_safety_threshold carries a factor of 1,0. The 0,02 tolerance is the 0,1 degC quantisation of BMS_T_Derate_Ref propagated through the 1/5 slope, plus the factor's own 0,001 step.
At and above the ceiling the factor is zero: every sample where BMS_T_Derate_Ref is at or above T_batt_max carries a factor of 0,0.
The ramp is linear, pinned at the midpoint of the band: over the 57,0 degC to 58,0 degC slice of BMS_T_Derate_Ref the mean factor is 0,50, which is what (60 - 57,5) / 5 gives.

The derated limit is the bound the current respects: wherever the published BMS_I_Chg_Lim is at or below 30 A, BMS_I_Dc is not below -30 A. The 0,15 A tolerance is the sum of the two signals' quantisation steps.
A fully derated limit stops the charge: wherever BMS_I_Chg_Lim is zero, no charging current flows.

items.exit_criteria: The terminal-to-open-circuit difference at the budget is reported together with the time at which it crosses the 2,0 V tolerance.
items.notes: EXPECTED TO FAIL, on C1. The plant's slow diffusion time constant TAU2 is rigged from 600 s to 900 s, which is longer than the relaxation budget the requirement allows. At the Sleep entry the RC2 branch carries 0,05 ohm x 150 A x (1 - e^-1) = 4,74 V; 600 s later it still carries 4,74 x e^(-600/900) = 2,43 V against the 2,0 V tolerance, and it does not cross that tolerance until 777 s. The fast RC1 branch has a 1 s time constant and is gone within 5 s of the entry, so it contributes nothing. VOCABULARY LIMITATION: |BMS_U_Dc - BMS_U_Ocv_Est| <= 2,0 V is a signal-versus-signal comparison the vocabulary cannot express; gate C2 pins the open-circuit estimate at 771,0 V over the evaluation window, which turns the difference into the absolute bound C1 uses.
items.objective: Show that after the battery system enters Sleep the terminal voltage converges to the open-circuit estimate within t_transient_Voltage_sec = 600 s.

pass_criteria.description: At the Sleep entry plus t_transient_Voltage_sec, the terminal voltage is within 2,0 V of the 771,0 V open-circuit estimate, so it is at or above 769,0 V. The 2,0 V tolerance is 0,24 % of the 840 V rail and one sixtieth of the 120 V open-circuit span, which is 1,7 points of SOC if the reading were used to recalibrate.
The relaxation is monotone: the terminal voltage never falls during the Sleep residency, which pins the direction of the decay as well as its size.

gates.description: The Sleep residency starts at t = 900 s and lasts to the end of the run, so the relaxation budget fits inside it.

The open-circuit estimate is constant at 771,0 V through the relaxation, because no current flows and the technical SOC therefore does not move. This is what licenses writing the 2,0 V tolerance as an absolute bound on BMS_U_Dc.

preconditions.prose: The run must enter Sleep at t = 900 s and stay there for the full 600 s budget, and the open-circuit estimate must be stationary over the evaluation window.

steps.action: Read the terminal voltage over the second ending at t = 1 500 s, which is the Sleep entry plus the 600 s budget.
steps.expected: It is at or above 769,0 V, so it sits within 2,0 V of the open-circuit estimate.

steps.action: Take the sample-to-sample derivative of the terminal voltage over the relaxation.
steps.expected: It is never negative: under the battery convention the terminal voltage was depressed by the RC branches during discharge and rises toward the open-circuit voltage as they decay.

items.title: Terminal voltage relaxes to the open-circuit voltage within the budget

items.entry_criteria: The run's BTMS_01 group decodes and carries both heater signals.
items.exit_criteria: All three criteria PASS and the dwell in each heater state is reported.
items.notes: EXPECTED VERDICT: PASS. The plant's HEATER_POWER_LOW and HEATER_POWER_HIGH are overridden to 500 W and 2 000 W in every scenario, so the heat the model actually injects and the BTMS_P_Heater value on the bus are the same number; publishing 500 / 2 000 while the plant heated with its stock 2 500 / 5 000 would make the temperature rise disagree with the published power, which is a failure indistinguishable from a bug. BTMS_Heater_State is the state the heater is running, one tick behind BTMS_Heater_Req, so the power and the state describe the same instant.
items.objective: Show that the heater offers exactly the states 0, 1 and 2, that each delivers 0 W, P_heater_middle = 500 W and P_heater_max = 2000 W respectively, and that all three are occupied in the run.

pass_criteria.description: State 0 is off: every sample of a heater-off residency of at least 1 s carries 0 W. The window's min_duration_s is what makes this criterion also assert that the state is occupied.
State 1 delivers P_heater_middle: every sample of a state-1 residency of at least 1 s carries 500 W.
State 2 delivers P_heater_max: every sample of a state-2 residency of at least 1 s carries 2 000 W.

gates.description: The heater state never leaves the three specified values: the maximum over the run is 2.

preconditions.prose: The run must exercise a cold soak deep enough to occupy all three heater states; a run that never heats leaves two of the three mappings unverified.

steps.action: Decode BTMS_01 and read BTMS_Heater_State and BTMS_P_Heater at 10 Hz.
steps.expected: Both are present; the power is in watts.

steps.action: Window the run on each heater state in turn, requiring at least 1 s of residency, and read the heater power over each window.
steps.expected: State 0 delivers 0 W, state 1 delivers 500 W and state 2 delivers 2 000 W, each within 1 W over every sample of its residency.

stimulus.notes: Cold soak at -10 degC ambient from a 20 degC pack with no traction current. The plant's KE is raised to 40 W/degC, the cold-soak loss coefficient of an uninsulated pack in a draught; with the stock 1,6 W/degC a 20 degC pack needs 2 166 s just to fall to 5 degC, longer than the whole trace.

items.title: Heater provides the three specified power states

items.entry_criteria: The run's BMS_03 and BTMS_01 groups decode and are on the same trace.
items.exit_criteria: The time spent below T_batt_min in a heater state other than 2 is reported whether the criteria pass or fail.
items.notes: EXPECTED TO FAIL. The controller calibration HEAT2_ON, the state-2 entry threshold, is rigged from T_batt_min = 5 degC to 3 degC, two kelvin too low. The pack therefore sits below 5 degC on the 500 W stage, which cannot hold it: against the 40 W/degC cold-soak loss at -10 degC ambient, 500 W settles at 2,5 degC. The violation lasts roughly 277 s of the 600 s run. Under the correct law the same scenario limit-cycles between 5 degC and 8 degC and never sits below 5 degC outside state 2, so the threshold is the only difference. BAT-SYS-TC-009 still passes on the same trace, because all three heater states are occupied and each delivers its specified power.
items.objective: Show that whenever the battery temperature is below T_batt_min = 5 degC the battery system commands heater state 2, so the fastest available recovery to the permitted window is used.

pass_criteria.description: Below the minimum temperature the heater is at maximum: every sample where BMS_T_Batt is at or below 4,9 degC carries heater state 2. The threshold is set one quantisation step inside T_batt_min so the window cannot straddle the 0,1 degC step at exactly 5,0 degC.
The commanded state is backed by the power: every sample below the minimum temperature carries P_heater_max = 2 000 W.

gates.description: The pack really falls below T_batt_min, so the unwanted condition the requirement guards against actually occurs.

preconditions.prose: The run must take the pack below 5 degC. A cold soak that never reaches the threshold leaves the requirement untested, and the 40 W/degC cold-soak loss coefficient is what makes that reachable inside 600 s.

steps.action: Decode BMS_03 and BTMS_01 and read BMS_T_Batt, BTMS_Heater_State and BTMS_P_Heater.
steps.expected: All three are present with the units of BATTERY_DC_V1.

steps.action: Window the run on BMS_T_Batt at or below 4,9 degC and read the heater state over that window.
steps.expected: It is 2 at every sample.

steps.action: Read the heater power over the same window.
steps.expected: It is 2 000 W at every sample.

stimulus.notes: Cold soak at -10 degC ambient from a 20 degC pack with no traction current. The plant's KE is raised to 40 W/degC, the cold-soak loss coefficient of an uninsulated pack in a draught; with the stock 1,6 W/degC a 20 degC pack needs 2 166 s just to fall to 5 degC, longer than the whole trace.

items.title: Heater commanded to maximum below the minimum battery temperature

notes: Ten system test cases, one per BAT-SYS requirement, evaluated against the four MF4 bus-log traces battery-trace-gen produces: T1 carries TC-001, TC-002 and TC-003; T2 carries TC-004, TC-005 and TC-006; T3 carries TC-007 and TC-008; T4 carries TC-009 and TC-010. Four of the ten are EXPECTED TO FAIL - TC-003, TC-006, TC-008 and TC-010 - each for a declared, rigged parameter named in its own notes and in out/manifest.json, and each failure is a genuine violation of the stated limit in the trace content rather than a missing channel or a broken signal. Every current criterion is written in battery sign: positive = discharge, negative = charge, which is the convention the BMS_I_Dc channel comment states and the only place a reader of the decoded lake can recover it. channel_group carries CAN frame names rather than raster group names, because frame_name is what the lake holds for a bus-logging file. Three cases document a vocabulary limitation in their notes - TC-002, TC-004, TC-006 and TC-008 all need a signal-versus-signal comparison that rule.value, a number, cannot express - and are decomposed into numeric bounds valid at named operating points. No threshold appears in prose only; the description fields are display text and carry no bound the evaluator needs. impl_ref is null on all ten: the Python implementations are authored separately and the sha256 of a file this document has not seen must not be asserted here.
